response.query: How should cuts interact with relax‑and‑fix practically: which to globalize, how lazy callbacks affect block solves/branching, and when to disable expensive cuts?
response.answer: Lazy callbacks add constraints as nodes expand; user cuts are optional and can be used for tighter bounds. Expensive cuts should be disabled when branching to avoid inefficiency. Use lazy constraints for immediate node pruning.

results.content:
Title: OR in an OB World: User Cuts versus Lazy Constraints
The user is somewhat charitably assumed to know what she or he is doing, so a user-injected solution is assumed to satisfy all lazy constraints.) What changed in the refactoring of the cut callback interface is that lazy constraints are checked *only* when a candidate solution is found. Since user cut callbacks are not called when candidate incumbents are found, at least for Benders decomposition this would suggest adding the same cut generation logic in both a lazy constraint callback (mandatory) and a user cut callback (optional). Should you add a lazy constraint in the callback that cuts off the candidate, CPLEX rejects the candidate and (as I understand it) adds the new lazy constraint (either locally or globally, depending on how you added it), makes it active, and starts over at the node (solving the node LP and, in the process, repeating the cut cycle -- so if you also have a user cut callback, I think it will be called again at the node). But when the lazy constraint is used by callback, the cut will be added when a candidate node in search tree is found. You refer to the legality of adding lazy constraint from a user cut callback. Thanks so much for your sharing, it really helps me a lot.when I tried to use Java to call CPLEX and use callback functions to solve a VRP problem with branch-and-cut ,some problems emerged.I took out the subtour elimination constraint from the original problem, and used it as usercut and lazyconstraint .When I only used it as a lazyconstraint,the algorithm worked out very well, but when I used it as both usercut and lazyconstraint Java program couldn't stop, it kept calling usercutCallback at node0 and wouldn't make branch. Regarding your first question, let me start by saying that I would use both callbacks with different cuts in each (Benders cuts in the lazy constraint callback, bound-tightening cuts in the user cut callback) if I had a recipe for generating bound tightening cuts. I once did an experiment in which I added the Benders cuts in a lazy constraint callback, queued them within my code, and then added them again in a user cut callback.

Title: When does Gurobi add cuts from callback - Operations Research Stack Exchange
#### Stack Exchange Network. Stack Exchange network consists of 183 Q&A communities including Stack Overflow, the largest, most trusted online community for developers to learn, share their knowledge, and build their careers. ### more stack exchange communities. # When does Gurobi add cuts from callback. A while ago I used Gurobi and I added user cuts from within a callback. However, I got the feeling that my user cuts were not directly added to the model. ## 2 Answers 2. Assuming you are using more than a single thread, then Gurobi performs all work you code in the callbacks with a single thread. All remaining threads process the branch and bound nodes (without doing the callbacks). When your user cuts are added is then determined by some black box magic of Gurobi. Then, 3 of the threads are processing branch&bound nodes. If a particular branch&bound node is processed and there are valid inequalities (i.e. user cuts) to be separated, it is put in a pool of such nodes. Now suppose that some valid inequalities are separated by this thread for some particular branch & bound node. As these processes (of processing callbacks on the one hand and branch&bounding on the other hand) are more or less independent (which is what I presume, but please correct me if I am wrong), it is left to Gurobi to when/how to add the separated inequalities. While lazy constraints must be added each time a node is expanded at a branch-and-bound tree, a solver is not obligated to add user cuts at any point in time; it chooses when to add user cuts. If you want Gurobi to add them immediately, you are better off adding lazy constraints. See here:  for more details on the differences between the two approaches (note that CPLEX and Gurobi actually implement callbacks quite differently, so the blog post won't be entirely accurate for Gurobi). ## Your Answer. results.title: Implementing Lazy Constraints (Java)
results.content: FICO Xpress Optimization: User Forum. We are interested in using Lazy Constraints in Xpress (Java) to implement a TSP algorithm. In particular, after each integer solution is generated, we would like to search for violated constraints and add the needed cuts if necessary. You need to be careful about not using destructive presolve (you seem to be trying to add constraints on variables that have been removed by presolve):. With the Xpress-Optimizer, you could implement "lazy constraints" as "delayed rows" (see XPRSloaddelayedrows; or if you are using a modelling tool for stating your problem: Mosel: defdelayedrows, BCL C: XPRBsetdelayed) - however, this means that you need to state all constraints upfront which certainly is impractical in the context of TSP. Regarding the use of Optimizer callbacks from Java, please take a look at the examples FICO Xpress Examples Repository: Demonstrates setting up and using callbacks (. ) and FICO Xpress Examples Repository: Els - An economic lot-sizing problem solved by cut-and-branch and branch-and-cut heuris… (. One of the Mosel examples implements a subtour elimination algorithm for TSP, looping over complete MIP solves: FICO Xpress Examples Repository: Air transport (. which is extended to a heuristic for larger instances in this version of the example: FICO Xpress Examples Repository: Solving the TSP problem by a series of optimization subproblems. Below I am attaching an alternative Mosel implementation of the TSP subproblem solving that uses MIP callbacks: if your initial problem statement does not correspond to the full problem and you wish to use the cut manager to add further constraints during the MIP search you need to configure the solver correspondingly (in particular, disable dual reductions). The above code is being used to detect any violated constraint and add the lazy constraints. It is not possible to define new constraints (XPRBctr) for a problem during the MIP search, instead you need to create cuts (XPRBcut) and add them to the problem via XPRBprob.addcuts. Exception in thread "main" : (addcuts) Xpress-Optimizer error 405 during 'addcuts'. All cuts are valid for the problem, but maybe Xpress doesn't like them since the current solution to be accepted is violated by them.

Problem using user cuts and lazy constraints callbacks together#1206. ## Description. opened on Mar 20, 2018. I have implemented a branch-and-cut framework in julia (solving with Gurobi) and I use both user cuts and lazy constraints callbacks. After defining the MILP, the structure of the code is as follows:. function mycutgenerator #some user cuts # end function mylazygenerator #some lazy constraints # end addcutcallback addlazycallback solve. As a first step, I have added an empty lazy constraints callback (no lazy constraints added) after the user cuts callback. In this case, since no lazy constraints are added at any node of the B&B tree, I was expecting to get the same solution I would get if I were to only call user cuts. Nevertheless, I have noticed that the solver (Gurobi) provides a different solution. Adding the empty lazy constraints callback to the user cuts callback I get:. Optimal solution found (tolerance 1.00e-04). Best objective 2.977717854818e+02, best bound 2.977717854818e+02, gap 0.0000%. Without the empty lazy callback (only user cuts callback) I get:. Optimal solution found (tolerance 1.00e-04). Best objective 2.881945379299e+02, best bound 2.881945379299e+02, gap 0.0000%. Any idea of why this is happening?
